title: LRU Cache
prompt:
Design a Least-Recently-Used cache with O(1) `get` and `put`:

- `LRUCache(int capacity)`
- `int get(int key)` — value, or `-1` if absent; counts as a use
- `void put(int key, int value)` — insert/update; if over capacity, evict the least-recently-used key

The standard design: a HashMap for O(1) lookup plus a doubly linked list ordering keys by recency (most-recent at the front, LRU at the back).

tests.note: updating an existing key refreshes it and doesn't evict

hints: HashMap<Integer, Node> for lookup; a doubly linked list with dummy head/tail for recency order.
On get/put of an existing key: unlink the node and move it to the front (most recent).
On put when full: evict the node just before the tail (the LRU), and remove it from the map.

solution.explanation: The HashMap gives O(1) key→node access; the doubly linked list gives O(1) reordering and eviction. Every access moves its node to the front, so the node adjacent to the tail is always the least-recently-used. (Java's LinkedHashMap with accessOrder=true is a shortcut, but the manual DLL is what interviews expect.)
